subject: Post-call: GDPR next steps — DPA, SCC module & role alignment for Acme Health
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lisa Greene <lisa.greene@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Dec 2025 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: GDPR next steps — DPA, SCC module & role alignment for Acme Health

Hi Lisa,

Thanks again for taking the time on the call this morning — really appreciated the context on Acme Health's workload (clinical summaries ingestion + anonymized analytics) and the compliance checkpoints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of what we covered:
- Primary data flows: customer uploads PHI-adjacent clinical notes into your S3 tenant; Acme will submit inference jobs to Redwood; results are stored in your environment.
- Compliance asks: you flagged GDPR DPA, EU SCC module selection, SOC 2 Type II report, and a potential BAA depending on PHI scope.
- Timeline: you indicated procurement + legal review in ~2–3 weeks.

Immediate asks (action items):
1) Can you confirm whether Acme Health will act as the data controller for the clinical notes (my understanding: yes)? This will determine SCC module selection (controller -> processor vs controller -> controller).
2) Attached is a short vendor security questionnaire you mentioned — we received it during the call. Please confirm any answers on your side and we can fill any gaps. (Attachment: Acme-Vendor-Security-Questionnaire-20251210.pdf)
3) We attached a Redwood DPA draft for initial review. If Acme prefers SCC Module 2 (Controller -> Processor), the draft aligns to that approach; let us know if your legal team prefers Module 1 mapping. (Attachment: Redwood-DPA-draft-v1.docx)
4) I’ll loop in our security and legal leads to provide SOC 2 evidence and confirm BAA posture if PHI is in-scope.

Desired next steps / timeline:
- Please confirm controller role (controller/processor) by EOD Friday 12/12 so we can scope the correct SCC module.
- If you want a joint legal call to walk the DPA/SCC options, we can schedule next week.

Thanks — I’m putting Aisha and Dev on copy to pick up the SOC2/technical questions.

Best,

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0118

---
Attachments: Acme-Vendor-Security-Questionnaire-20251210.pdf, Redwood-DPA-draft-v1.docx
From: Lisa Greene <lisa.greene@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Dec 2025 12:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: GDPR next steps — DPA, SCC module & role alignment for Acme Health

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the quick answers you requested: 

1) Acme Health is the data controller for the clinical notes dataset; Redwood would be a processor for the inference workflow.
2) We did attach the vendor questionnaire — I expect our security ops to kick that off formally; I’ve CC'd vendor-security@acmehealth.com for tracking.
3) Please treat Module 2 (Controller -> Processor) as the default SCC module we expect. If your DPA maps to Module 2, that will speed review.

Additional requests from Procurement / Security: 
- SOC 2 Type II report (latest) and any SOC 3/public summary you can share.
- A short note on encryption at rest and in transit, and key management (KMS/HSM) — especially whether we can bring our own KMS in a private deployment.
- If PHI is in-scope, confirm whether Redwood will sign a BAA or if Acme requires supplemental contractual language.

We’ll aim to get you feedback on the questionnaire and any redlines to the DPA by 12/19. If you can surface the SOC2 link and a short KMS write-up, that would help accelerate our side.

Thanks,
Lisa Greene
Director, Cloud Compliance — Acme Health
lisa.greene@acmehealth.com

Jordan / team — thanks for the ping and the clear ask. Short answers and next steps below.

SCC module & role alignment:
- Given Acme confirmed controller role, we recommend proceeding with Module 2 (Controller -> Processor). That is the standard mapping and matches our DPA draft.

SOC 2 & encryption / KMS:
- SOC 2 Type II: we can share a redacted report via secure link (see: https://redwood-inference.securefiles/soc2/type2-report). I’ve started the access request for lisa.greene@acmehealth.com — please confirm the email they want added for delivery.
- Encryption: All hosted data is encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.3). In Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) with KMS/HSM integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). I’ll attach a one-page KMS capability note by EOD.

BAA / PHI:
- If PHI is in-scope, Redwood is willing to discuss BAA terms. There are operational requirements (dedicated logging, retention configuration, and minimum Private deployment controls) we’ll need to enumerate. I’ll loop in Legal if Acme confirms PHI will be processed.

Next steps / ownership:
- Jordan: confirm which Acme email we should add to the SOC2 share link (we need an exact address).
- Dev: please prep the one-page KMS/Private-deployment note and attach to the questionnaire answers.
- Aisha (me): I’ll review the DPA draft for Module 2 alignment, mark any high-level legal flags, and return a redline by COB 12/16.

We can also propose a 30-min technical + legal working session the week of 12/22 if Acme’s timeline requires.

Aisha Rahman
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com
